The algorithm has been implemented in C++ programming language.<\/jats:p>","DOI":"10.4018\/ijse.2018070106","type":"journal-article","is-referenced-by-count":2,"title":["An Approach to Opinion Mining in Community Graph Using Graph Mining Techniques"],"author":[{"ORCID":"https:\/\/orcid.org\/0000-0002-2781-9708","authenticated-orcid":true,"given":"Bapuji","family":"Rao","sequence":"first","affiliation":[{"name":"Indira Gandhi Institute of Technology, Sarang, India"}],"role":[{"vocabulary":"crossref","role":"author"}]}],"container-title":["International Journal of Synthetic Emotions"],"issued":{"date-parts":[[2018,7]]},"URL":"https:\/\/doi.org\/10.4018\/ijse.2018070106"},{"abstract":"<jats:p>Under the influence of extreme weather, the risk of urban flooding is constantly rising. Social media, with its characteristics of immediacy and wide participation, has become an important data source for flood emergency decision-making. However, online public opinions on urban flood disasters not only rise and fall along with the rainfall rhythm during the flood season, but also are interrelated and interact with each other among platforms, communities and topics. The existing methods are difficult to depict these two types of patterns simultaneously. For this reason, This study proposes a flood-season rhythm-aware Petri graph spatio-temporal convolution model. By dividing the hydrological flood season, a public opinion Petri net model for flood season rhythm modulation is established, and a three-layer heterogeneous graph of \"platform-user-topic\" is constructed to generate public opinion prediction results. For a 184-day flood-season case of a riverside city in the middle Yangtze River basin, evaluated by a five-fold rolling-origin backtest over 20 random seeds, the proposed model attains RMSE, MAE and MAPE of 8.30, 6.01 and 12.57% at a 1-day horizon, outperforming all benchmark methods and reducing RMSE by 18.2%, 9.4% and 4.8% relative to persistence, dynamic time-weighted entropy and STGCN, respectively; it remains optimal in MAE and MAPE at a 3-day horizon. Ablation experiments attribute accuracy gains of 17.7%, 4.8% and 2.9% to the rainfall forecast, the rhythm modulation and the three-layer heterogeneous graph, respectively. Recently, graph representation learning methods based on node embedding have drawn attention in Recommender systems such as Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs) that is powerful method for collaborative filtering. The GCN performs neighborhood aggregation mechanism to extract high level representation for both user and items. In this paper, we propose a recommendation algorithm based on node similarity convolutional matrices with topological property in GCNs where the linkage measure is illustrated as a bipartite graph. The experiments indicate the necessity of capturing user\u2013item graph structure in recommendation.
